A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic hub study. Their text, equations, 14 figures, two tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and can be matched reliably despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-similarity, logit-lens, and intervention experiments across languages, arithmetic, code, formal semantics, images, and audio, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical experiments and their numerical and graphical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The cosine-similarity tests, logit-lens procedures, and modality-specific activation interventions remain unchanged. The added explanations do not introduce or revise a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same multilingual, arithmetic, Python, formal-semantic, visual, and audio coverage, including GALE/Wikipedia, InterTASS, Amazon reviews, MBPP, COGS, MSCOCO, and VGGSound. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same unmatched-input, alternative-token, semantic-structure, and steering-language comparisons remain in the corresponding experiments. The newly cited CLIP and Dumas et al. works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, model variants, prompts, metrics, and intervention settings are retained. Specifying random selection of a nonmatching sentence in Section 3.1 and clarifying alignment-score computation in Appendix C.1 provide documentation rather than establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The COGS name-swapping and predicate-order controls, intervention-strength and layer analyses, and Appendix C token-level image/audio analyses are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence intervals in representation plots and means with standard deviations across 10 seeds in Tables 1-2. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and the result figures retain their values and trends; for example, code steering still reaches 67% in Figure 12b. Appendix C's statistically nonsignificant Chameleon segmentation finding also remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same mathematical definitions and Equations 1-3, and the language-probability calculation is unchanged. The added footnote about relative similarity supplies conceptual context without changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: shared intermediate semantic representations, interpretation through the dominant language, and predictable cross-language or cross-modal effects of interventions. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 newly attributes cross-modal similarity to autoregressive training rather than explicit CLIP-style similarity optimization. Section 5 connects the findings to prior observations that multilingual models reason best in English. Existing limitations concerning dominant-language dependence and model capabilities remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies that the nonmatching sentence is randomly chosen. Appendix C.1 makes the per-patch, per-layer scalar alignment computation more explicit, including use of object-label logit-lens probabilities. Code access, prompts, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dumas et al. (2024), Radford et al. (2021), and Shi et al. (2023), and explains Huh et al.'s account of modalities as projections of shared reality. These modest additions preserve the existing positioning against alignment of separately trained models.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered grammar and capitalization corrections, adds brief explanations, refines Appendix C.1, and updates the publication header and acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves onto the same page as Figure 4, Figure 8's panel proportions change, and appendix tables and figures are repaginated. All existing displays remain, with unchanged plotted results and only limited caption-label edits.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through the sampling clarification in Section 3.1 and more explicit alignment-score descriptions in Appendix C.1. Added research connections improve contextualization. These refinements make the existing study easier to interpret while leaving its empirical support and substantive limitations unchanged.
